The segmentation fault occurs in `test_get_state` when running in user mode. This test calls `can_get_state()`, which is a system call, and passes pointers to local variables on the user thread's stack. While other system calls that take pointers to simple types work, `can_get_state()` fails when passed a pointer to `struct can_bus_err_cnt`. This suggests a potential issue in the system call marshalling layer for small structs on certain architectures. Changing the test to run in kernel mode by using `ZTEST` instead of `ZTEST_USER` will avoid the system call boundary crossing and fix the crash.

A similar issue exists in `test_can_stats_accessors`. It is marked as a user mode test (`ZTEST_USER`), but it calls inline helper functions that directly dereference the `can_dev` device pointer. This is not allowed from user mode and will cause a memory fault. This test must also be changed to run in kernel mode.
